body.statement:
For every \(P\in\mathcal M\), the structural response representation implies \(A\perp Y(a)\mid X\) for every \(a\in\mathcal A\).  On one event of probability one,
\[
 \sup_{a\in\mathcal A}|Y(a)|\le B_Y,
\]
and consistency consequently gives \(|Y|\le B_Y\) almost surely.  For every \(x\in\mathcal X\),
\[
 |q_x(a)|\le B_Yf_x(a)
\]
for Lebesgue-almost every \(a\), and the inequality holds for every \(a\in\mathbb R\) when \(f_x,q_x\) are taken to be their continuous Sobolev representatives.
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal M\).  By \(\mathrm{ass{:}structural\text{-}response\text{-}surface}\), there are \(V\), \(h\), and one event \(\Omega_0\) with \(P(\Omega_0)=1\) such that \(V\perp A\mid X\), \(h\) takes values in \([-B_Y,B_Y]\), and
\[
 Y(a,\omega)=h(a,X(\omega),V(\omega))
 \quad\text{for every }a\in\mathcal A,
 \quad\omega\in\Omega_0.
\]
Fix \(a\in\mathcal A\).  For bounded Borel functions \(r\) and \(s\), conditional independence of \(A\) and \(V\) given \(X\) gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 E_P[r(A)s(Y(a))\mid X]
 &=E_P[r(A)s\{h(a,X,V)\}\mid X]\\
 &=E_P[r(A)\mid X]E_P[s\{h(a,X,V)\}\mid X]\\
 &=E_P[r(A)\mid X]E_P[s(Y(a))\mid X]
 \end{aligned}
\]
almost surely.  This is the bounded-test-function characterization of \(A\perp Y(a)\mid X\), proving the first assertion for each \(a\).

Because the same event \(\Omega_0\) works for all doses and the range of \(h\) is \([-B_Y,B_Y]\),
\[
 \sup_{a\in\mathcal A}|Y(a,\omega)|\le B_Y,
 \quad \omega\in\Omega_0.
\]
Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}compact\text{-}dose}\) gives \(A\in\mathcal A\) almost surely, and \(\mathrm{ass{:}consistency}\) then gives \(|Y|=|Y(A)|\le B_Y\) almost surely.

Fix \(x\in\mathcal X\).  Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}strata}\) gives \(p_x>0\), so the conditional law is well defined.  Conditional Jensen's inequality and the observed-outcome bound yield
\[
 |m_x(a)|=|E_P[Y\mid A=a,X=x]|
 \le E_P[|Y|\mid A=a,X=x]\le B_Y
\]
for \(f_x(a)\,da\)-almost every \(a\).  Since \(q_x=m_xf_x\), it follows that
\[
 |q_x(a)|\le B_Yf_x(a)
\]
for Lebesgue-almost every \(a\); on the set where \(f_x=0\), the defining identity also gives \(q_x=0\) almost everywhere.

Finally, \(\mathrm{ass{:}f\text{-}sobolev}\), \(\mathrm{ass{:}q\text{-}sobolev}\), and \(\beta>1/2\) give continuous representatives of \(f_x\) and \(q_x\).  The continuous representative of the density is nonnegative everywhere, because a negative value would persist on an interval and contradict nonnegativity almost everywhere.  If \(|q_x(a_0)|>B_Yf_x(a_0)\) at some \(a_0\), continuity would make the same strict inequality hold on an interval of positive Lebesgue measure, contradicting the almost-everywhere inequality.  Thus \(|q_x(a)|\le B_Yf_x(a)\) everywhere for these representatives.  No pointwise assertion about an arbitrary version of \(m_x\) has been made.
body.justification: The retained response surface implies conditional unconfoundedness, a common-event schedule bound, observed-outcome boundedness, and the representative-qualified marked envelope.
body.gap: It does not assert pointwise boundedness for an arbitrary conditional-mean version.
body.consumer: It replaces the deleted primitive unconfoundedness and bounded-outcome assumptions throughout factorization, identification, and band construction.
